root_idea.summary: The root has two closely related semantic orientations: darkness or the absence of light, and placing something outside its proper position or due.
root_idea.development: From the latter orientation developed the meanings of transgression, injustice, deprivation, and wrongful treatment; from the former developed darkness and figurative darkness such as ignorance, unbelief, and unrighteousness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Feminine active-participle forms belong to the same public lexical item.
This is an inflected oblique plural form of the active participle ظَالِم.

senses.definition: To wrong, act unjustly, injure, or transgress against someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used intransitively for acting wrongfully and transitively for wronging another; Quranic usage also includes wrongdoing against God, other people, or oneself.

senses.definition: To deprive, despoil, or cause loss of a due or right.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes causing someone to suffer loss; in the Quran, the verb can deny that God deprives anyone of even the smallest due.

senses.definition: To reject or disbelieve signs, thereby treating them wrongfully.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-attested construction with بِ; the object may be understood as the signs or as those wronged because of them.

senses.definition: To become dark or enter into darkness.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence the verb is used of darkness coming upon or surrounding them; its transitivity is discussed in the classical evidence.

senses.definition: More or most wrongful, unjust, or transgressive.
senses.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective used to identify the graver instance of wrongdoing or the more unjust claimant or act.

senses.definition: One who wrongs, acts unjustly, injures, or transgresses; a wrongdoer.
senses.usage_conditions: The active participle functions adjectivally or substantivally and is used for wrongdoing against God, people, or oneself; gender and case forms are included under this headword.

senses.definition: Greatly or repeatedly wrongful; intensely unjust.
senses.usage_conditions: An intensive adjective describing a pronounced or recurring disposition to wrongdoing.

senses.definition: One who wrongs greatly, repeatedly, or habitually.
senses.usage_conditions: An intensive epithet; in the Quran it occurs in a negation concerning God's not wronging His servants.
A verbal noun and abstract noun covering transgression against God, another person, or oneself; the Quran also uses it for associating partners with God and for wrongful deprivation or treatment.

senses.definition: Darknesses; conditions or regions lacking light.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural may describe physical darkness, including the three darknesses associated with gestation; it can also describe successive or surrounding layers of darkness.

senses.definition: Figurative darknesses of ignorance, unbelief, polytheism, sin, or unrighteousness.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic metaphor contrasted with light and guidance; the physical and figurative readings are distinguished by context.

senses.definition: Wronged, treated unjustly, injured, or deprived of a due.
senses.usage_conditions: A passive participle for the victim or object of wrongdoing; it may qualify a person who has been killed or otherwise treated wrongfully.

senses.definition: Darkening or being in darkness; darkened.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle related to أَظْلَمَ, used in the Quran for beings or surroundings characterized by darkness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wronging another or engaging in mutual wronging as an intended act.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for desiring another person's wronging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impose on someone a demand or burden beyond his power.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of someone being asked for something beyond his ability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slaughter an animal without disease or other stated cause.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-related usage, especially of slaughtering a camel sound enough not to require slaughter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cover or mate with a female animal prematurely or against her inclination.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a she-camel or to a male donkey mating with a female before the proper time or while she is pregnant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drink or give milk before it has thickened and yielded its butter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of taking the contents of a milk-skin or giving such immature milk to people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do something hastily, before its proper time or season.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived application of doing something outside its appropriate time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dig or make a watering place where digging is not appropriate; of water, to furrow or reach ground not reached before.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of ground, watering-troughs, valleys, and torrents when they extend into an uncustomary or previously untouched place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exceed the proper limit by adding foreign earth to a grave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic reproof addressed to people who add earth other than the grave's own.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn aside from the main or beaten path.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of deviating from a road or turning away from something rather than keeping to it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prevent or obstruct someone from doing something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Appears in constructions meaning “what has prevented you from it?”; related proverbial expressions describe an obstacle that misplaces an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To accuse someone of wrongdoing or attribute wrongdoing to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II usage meaning to declare or impute that someone is a wrongdoer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To obtain justice for a person from his wrongdoer and aid him against that wrongdoer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II causative or remedial usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To complain of being wronged to an authority or judge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The normal Form V complaint construction takes the alleged wrong to a judge or other adjudicator.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take the responsibility for wrongdoing upon oneself or claim it as one's own.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of the Form V; the lexical evidence records disagreement about this analysis.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat one another wrongfully or unjustly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal Form VI usage describing mutual wrongdoing among a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of goats, to strike one another with their horns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative animal usage attributed to their fatness, abundance of pasture, and liveliness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take upon oneself or bear wrong despite difficulty or the ability to resist.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form VIII describes enduring wrong willingly or with hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lustre or brightness of gold and of teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of teeth, the word can refer to a clear, intense lustre or whiteness that appears almost dark by contrast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Snow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported lexical use, also appearing in an expression about the brightness or “water” of the teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression أَدْنَى ظَلَم, the first or nearest thing encountered by sight, or nearness itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase may refer to the first obstruction of vision, a nearby person or object, or the onset of confused darkness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage with the plural ظُلُوم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The three especially dark nights following the three nights called دُرَع in a lunar month.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical calendrical name; the form and singular are described as morphologically anomalous by some authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Darkness, the absence or departure of light, or the beginning of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes an intensely dark night and adverbial expressions meaning at night or at the time of night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figurative ignorance, polytheism, transgression, or hardship and affliction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The darkness metaphor is opposed to light and guidance; ظُلُمَاتُ البحر can idiomatically mean the troubles or calamities of the sea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small, scant, mean, paltry, or of little worth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival usage describing small quantity or contemptible value.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sidelong or hostile glance from the outer angle of the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an idiomatic expression for looking at someone with anger or aversion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman accustomed to giving milk before it has matured and yielded its butter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intensive epithet applied in the cited expression to a woman and a milk-skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Milk drunk before it has thickened and its butter has emerged.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized epithet for immature milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Earth or soil dug in a place where digging was improper or where it had not previously been done.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also applied to earth taken from the lateral hollow of a grave and returned over the burial.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A male ostrich.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional explanation connects the name with making a nest or laying place in an improper location; another explanation connects it with supposed deafness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for certain stars, including stars associated with Sagittarius, Eridanus, or Piscis Austrinus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular and dual star names are reported with variant astronomical applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who often slaughters camels without disease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive animal-related specialization of habitual wrongful treatment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain grazed herb or strange tree, especially one with long shoots extending beyond the proper limit of its stem or root.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun distinct from the intensive adjective ظَلَّام.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who complains of his wrongdoer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported nominal use of ظَالِم in addition to its active-participle meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People who withhold, deny, or refuse others their rights or dues.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural collective designation for rights-deniers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An appellation of the ضَبّ lizard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the lizard's alleged eating of its young.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely black or deep in color, including hair or very green herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of darkness to intense blackness or deep green.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An evil or difficult day, or an affair whose way forward is obscure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied figuratively to hardship, calamity, or a matter whose proper course cannot be discerned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing or right of which someone has been defrauded, deprived, or wrongfully dispossessed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also denotes the claim or demand for restoration of that right; the plural is مَظَالِم, as in the expression for a day of claims for wrongfully taken things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A house or chamber decorated with pictures, gilding, or silvering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained either as putting decoration where it should not be or as displaying lustre.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Herbage spread over the ground without having been rained upon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of vegetation in an unusual or deficient condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The rukhkhām vulture and crows or ravens.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported bird-name usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land dug where digging was improper, where no digging had previously occurred, or where a well or watering-trough was made in an unsuitable place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same adjective is also applied to land on which rain has not fallen and which lacks pasture.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only reference to the next entry.
Entering darkness is covered by the Form IV darkness sense.
The exclamative use retains the same darkness meaning.
Further specifications of lustre and brightness.
The general noun meaning is covered by the Quranic verbal-noun sense.
Editorial correction of a mistaken form.
An intensely dark night is covered by the singular darkness meaning.
Further specifications of improperly dug earth.
The intensive wrongdoing meaning is represented under the Quranic intensive adjective senses.
The comparative wrongdoing meaning is represented under the Quranic adjective.
Becoming dark is represented by the Quranic active participle.
The general passive-participle meaning is represented under the Quranic form.

cautions: The Quranic material distinguishes physical darkness from figurative darkness; the latter is especially associated with ignorance, unbelief, polytheism, and unrighteousness.
The intensity implied by ظَلُوم and ظَلَّام is lexical, although contextual translations may render both simply as “unjust.”
The classical evidence records disagreement over whether أَظْلَمَ may be transitive as well as intransitive; the Quranic example is represented without resolving that broader grammatical issue.
